top_signal.title: 17-year-old planning to buy and operate a small motel at 18 — how realistic is this?
top_signal.summary: I’m 17 right now and graduating high school in about 8 months. I turn 18 in May 2027.  I’ve been seriously considering getting into small motel ownership as my first major business. I’m not expecting this to be easy, and I’m trying to figure out whether I’m being realistic or completely delusional.  My rough plan is:  Buy my first small motel around age 18–18.5  Ideally something around  $400k–$600k   Maybe something like  12–20 rooms   Find a private investor who could provide around  $100k  for the acquisition  Negotiate  seller financing  for the remaining balance rather than using a conventional bank  Ideally find a property with a  manager’s unit , which I would live in  Operate the motel myself initially  Handle the front desk, reservations, marketing, purchasing, basic management, etc.  Keep housekeeping payroll very low — potentially one part-time cleaner rather than a full staff  Modernize the property and improve the online presence, photos, website, social media, reviews, pricing, etc.  Eventually hire a manager once the motel produces enough cash flow that it makes sense  Then use the experience/equity/cash flow from the first property to acquire additional motels  I’m not expecting to sit around and collect checks from day one. I’m completely willing to work extremely hard in the beginning. I’m 18, so if I have to work 50–60 hours a week for a few years to build something, I’m fine with that.
